ideas.title: Dependency Storyteller
ideas.summary: Paste any dependency file and Claude generates a plain-English biography for each library, turning a wall of package names into a scannable 'cast of characters' for faster project onboarding.
ideas.description: A web tool where you paste a package.json, requirements.txt, or go.mod file and Claude generates a 'cast of characters' narrative, giving each dependency a short biography: what it does, why this project likely uses it, and any notable quirks or gotchas. The result is a scannable one-pager that turns a wall of library names into a readable story.
keyFeatures: Paste or upload dependency files (JSON, TOML, txt)
Per-dependency bio: purpose, common use cases, known footguns
Dependency category grouping (auth, UI, testing, data, etc.)
Copy as Markdown or export to PDF for team onboarding docs
ideas.whyInteresting: New contributors to a project spend hours reverse-engineering what each library does; this collapses that into a 30-second read. It also teaches students to think critically about why they reach for each dependency, not just how to install it.
ideas.inspiredBy: GitHub trending exploration of project onboarding pain points; HN discussions on making codebases approachable for new contributors

ideas.title: Live Code Annotation Station
ideas.summary: Students tap any line of a live-coded file on their phones to drop questions or confusion emojis in real time, giving the professor a live heatmap of where the class is getting lost, with an AI confusion summary at session end.
ideas.description: A lightweight web app professors share a link to at the start of a live coding session. Students open it on their phones or laptops, see a line-numbered view of the code being typed, and can tap any line to drop a question or confusion emoji in real time. A sidebar aggregates reactions as a live heatmap. At the end of the session, Claude summarizes the top confusion clusters with suggested re-explanations.
keyFeatures: Real-time line-by-line reaction and question dropping (no sign-in required for students)
Live heatmap sidebar showing which lines generated the most confusion
Professor view: questions stream in alongside the code as it is typed
Session-end AI summary of top confusion clusters with suggested re-explanations
ideas.techStack: React + Vite, Supabase Realtime, Tailwind, Claude API
ideas.whyInteresting: Most professors don't know which part of a live demo lost the class until the next exam. This surfaces confusion the moment it happens, making live coding sessions dramatically more responsive.
ideas.inspiredBy: Classroom engagement challenges during live coding lectures; HN 'Ask HN: What are you working on? (June 2026)' https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48528779

ideas.title: Agents From Scratch Workshop
ideas.summary: A multi-week assignment where students implement a minimal AI agent runtime from scratch in under 200 lines of Python, then use their own framework to build and demo one real-world agent.
ideas.description: A structured multi-week assignment where students implement a minimal AI agent loop in Python from scratch, targeting under 200 lines for the core runtime: tool registration, JSON tool-call parsing, context window management, and a multi-turn conversation loop. In the second half, students use their own mini-framework to build one useful agent and present a framework architecture diagram explaining their design decisions.
keyFeatures: Week 1-2: Implement the agent runtime (tool definitions, LLM call loop, error recovery)
Week 3: Add memory via sliding context window and a simple vector store for retrieval
Week 4: Build and demo one real agent using their own framework
Automated test harness that runs each student's agent against a suite of tool-use scenarios
ideas.techStack: Python, Flask (tool server), React + Vite (dashboard), Claude API or Gemini API, SQLite or ChromaDB
ideas.whyInteresting: Most CS students use agent frameworks as black boxes; building one from scratch forces them to confront every design decision that mature frameworks have already made, producing a much deeper understanding of how LLMs use tools and manage context.
ideas.inspiredBy: Hugging Face smolagents library philosophy of keeping agent core logic under 1,000 lines; https://dev.to/anmolbaranwal/open-source-toolkit-for-building-ai-agents-in-2026-55h1
